code.ac88f366f98e5d1f4e2859df1001d430bdb8364c: C2-ORCHESTRATION-CONFORMANCE-REPAIR correction: a party without the spec's probe makes no record (invariant III); prove types it PROBE_INVALID_SPEC.

1_commits.lane: c2/lane-o-orchestration (e3d0560 the change; ac88f36 the correction for invariant III in proof.py), merged at 6368ae57ec8ada335546bfd6ee979d98ed80615a; authorized by owner ruling 2026-09-30 B, Ruling 3 (C2-ORCHESTRATION-CONFORMANCE-REPAIR)

4_before: story_runner._probe(inputs, on_range, scratch) took the ONE factory of StoryInputs.probes and raised InvariantError('cycle 1 proves a story with exactly one probe factory') when there were more; both parties were built with a maker that never saw the spec being proved. StoryAdmission, in the same function, already resolved the probe per obligation by spec.probe_id.
5_after: story_runner._probe(inputs, on_range, scratch, spec) returns the factory registered under spec.probe_id, or None; Party(by_spec=True) hands the spec to its maker; prove() types a party without a probe for the spec as PROBE_INVALID_SPEC with no record. One ProductProof evaluation per obligation, by the probe its spec names; no result is cached or shared.
6_why_the_four_stories_could_not_execute: STORY-01-01, 03-01, 04-01 and 04-02 of PLAN-V2.2 carry specs of two or three probe kinds; admission needs every kind's factory wired, and with more than one factory wired the candidate stage raised the InvariantError — after the developer request had been spent (multi_kind_story.old)
7_required_because_new_probe_kinds_exist: YES: Cycle 1 had one probe kind, so 'the one factory' and 'the factory of the spec's probe' were the same object. The second kind made the candidate stage's shortcut observable. The change adds no probe, no protocol and no probe-specific branch.

scheduling.note: the order of stories is the caller's; run_story is AST-identical

StoryAdmission.note: byte-identical; it already selected the probe by spec.probe_id per obligation before the change

proof ordering.note: prove changed: implementer run -> its probe/evaluated -> verifier run -> its probe/evaluated -> proof/verified is preserved whenever both parties have a probe (the seven Cycle-1 corpus journals are identical under both kernels); when a party has none, nothing is measured and nothing is journaled before the typed failure

candidate freeze.note: AST/byte-identical; _attempt differs only in how the two Party objects are constructed

verifier agreement.note: verified_payload and the record comparison are byte-identical; prove's agreement branch is unchanged text

journal events.note: no event type, payload field or enum member added or changed. ONE measured difference in which events a failure path emits: see old_vs_new.post_merge_reproof_of_a_prior_story_s_spec_of_an_unwired_kind

projections.note: byte-identical; Q4 on the changed kernel: 100000/100000 matched against the six reference models, twice

failure taxonomy.note: byte-identical; prove uses the existing FailureCode.PROBE_INVALID_SPEC at one new site

9_identities.caveat: unchanged hashes show the specs and the plan did not move; they do not by themselves show orchestration semantics unchanged — items 8, 11, 12, 13 and old_vs_new carry that

12_cannot_silently_skip_a_probe.reading: an obligation whose probe is missing never commits: it is PROBE_INVALID at admission or PROBE_INVALID_SPEC at the proof; RFC §17's commit condition (a VerifiedProof per obligation) is evaluated by unchanged code

13_one_probe_cannot_satisfy_another_s_ob.mechanism: aisef2/probe/protocol.py run_probe (byte-identical) answers InvalidSpec when (spec.probe_id, spec.probe_digest) is not the probe's; each proof/verified binds its own spec_id, semantic_hash and its two records

14_generality.reading: the lookup is inputs.probes.get(spec.probe_id): any set of registered probes; the tests use synthetic two- and three-kind stories, permuted orders, and the four LedgerLock stories only as one case
